result.target_topic: Credit Card and Unsecured Revolving Loan Accrual and Charge-off Policies
result.target_summary: Credit cards and other unsecured revolving loans are not subject to non-accrual policies and continue to accrue interest until charged off at 180 days past due (DPD). Specific details regarding these charge-off policies are provided in a subsequent section.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: c_2024_8_D072 describes the non-accrual/charge-off policy for credit cards and unsecured revolving loans (accrue until 180 DPD then charged off). While c_2023_8_D029 mentioned the 180-day accrual rule, it was part of a broader consumer non-accrual section that also covered installment/real estate loans. c_2023_8_D032 covered charge-offs but did not explicitly link the 180-day accrual cessation to non-accrual status in the same focused manner as the current disclosure. The proposed group 0438 linked D072 to D029/D032, but D072 is specifically about the *non-accrual* status (or lack thereof) and timing of charge-off for unsecured lines, which is distinct from the installment non-accrual in D071. D029 covered both. Since D071 takes the installment part, D072 stands alone as the specific unsecured revolving non-accrual/charge-off policy, for which no single 2023 disclosure matches this specific focus (D029 was mixed, D032 was charge-off only).

comparisons.peer_topic: Nonperforming loan and charge-off criteria for credit card and unsecured consumer loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Credit card and other unsecured consumer loans are charged off at 180 days past due, or within 60 days of death, bankruptcy, or fraud confirmation. These loans continue to accrue interest until charged off and are not reported as nonperforming.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose that credit cards and other unsecured consumer loans continue to accrue interest until charged off and are not subject to non-accrual status. Citi specifies that charge-offs occur at 180 days past due (DPD), while Bank of America adds specific conditions for earlier charge-offs, such as within 60 days of death, bankruptcy, or fraud confirmation, in addition to the 180 DPD threshold.

sentences.text: Credit cards and other unsecured revolving loans generally are not subject to non-accrual policies and continue to accrue interest until charged off at 180 DPD.

Credit card and other unsecured consumer loans are charged off when the loan becomes 180 days past due, within 60 days after receipt of notification of death or bankruptcy or upon confirmation of fraud.
These loans continue to accrue interest until they are charged off and, therefore, are not reported as nonperforming loans.

comparisons.peer_summary: Credit card loans are charged off when 180 days past due, and installment loans are charged off when 120 days past due.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Citi both identify 180 days past due as the charge-off threshold for credit card loans. However, while Citi explicitly states that these loans are not subject to non-accrual policies and continue to accrue interest, Goldman Sachs' disclosure in this section focuses on the charge-off timing and mentions installment loans (120 DPD) without explicitly discussing the non-accrual/accrual status of the credit cards in the same sentence, though the 180-day metric is identical.

comparisons.peer_topic: Exemption for credit card loans from nonaccrual status
comparisons.peer_summary: Credit card loans are generally exempt from nonaccrual status per regulatory guidance, allowing interest and fees to continue accruing until charge-off or full payment.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan Chase disclose that credit card loans are exempt from non-accrual status and continue to accrue interest. Citi links this exemption to the general policy for unsecured revolving loans, while JPMorgan Chase explicitly cites regulatory guidance as the basis for this exemption. Both firms accrue interest until charge-off or full payment.

sentences.text: Credit cards and other unsecured revolving loans generally are not subject to non-accrual policies and continue to accrue interest until charged off at 180 DPD.

As permitted by regulatory guidance, credit card loans are generally exempt from being placed on nonaccrual status; accordingly, interest and fees related to credit card loans continue to accrue until the loan is charged off or paid in full.
